The first hour after waking sets the tone for the rest of the day, and a few consistent habits can meaningfully change how much energy you carry through the afternoon.

## Light exposure matters

Getting natural light within the first thirty minutes of waking helps regulate your circadian rhythm, which in turn affects alertness later in the day.

## Move before you scroll

Even a short walk or a few minutes of stretching before reaching for a phone tends to leave people feeling more alert than starting the day passively scrolling in bed.

## Hydrate before caffeine

A glass of water before coffee helps offset the mild dehydration that builds up overnight and can make that first cup of coffee more effective rather than less.

None of these habits need to take more than a few minutes, but stacking two or three of them consistently tends to produce a noticeably steadier energy curve than relying on caffeine alone.
